chunks: And he wrote to him regarding a man who had plots of lands, and departure to Mecca became imminent for him, while the village was several stages from his residence, and he did not have sufficient time to provide the boundaries of his land. So he identified the four boundaries of the village and said to the witnesses: Bear witness that I have sold to so-and-so — meaning the buyer — the whole village, one of whose boundaries is such-and-such, and the second, and the third, and the fourth. Yet he only had plots of land in this village. So is that valid for the buyer, while he only owns part of this village, though he has acknowledged it all for him?
So he, peace be upon him, wrote: It is not permissible to sell what one does not own; and the purchase has become binding from the seller only with respect to what he owns.

key_terms.بَيْعُ مَا لَيْسَ يَمْلِكُ: the sale of property that the seller does not own
key_terms.حُدُودَ الْقَرْيَةِ: the defining boundaries of the village used in the sale description
key_terms.قِطَاعُ أَرَضِينَ: separate plots of land owned within a larger area
key_terms.مَا يَمْلِكُ: that which the seller actually owns

ai.seo_question: Is a sale valid if someone sells more land than he actually owns?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the sale of property when the seller describes and sells more than he actually owns. The Imam عليه السلام states that selling what one does not own is invalid, while the sale remains effective only for the portion that truly belongs to the seller. It is significant in fiqh for defining the limits of lawful ownership and valid transfer in transactions.
